threads.subject: URGENT: confirm Q4 GPU budget lines before 16:00 board deck

messages.body:
Alex,

I'm finalising the board deck that goes up at 16:00 today. I need you to confirm the Q4 GPU expansion line items: hardware, hosting, and the contingency reserve. Please check they add up to the figure the board approved on 2 November.

If anything has moved since then, tell me before noon so I can adjust the slides. A short reply with the confirmed numbers is enough.

Sarah

Alex,

For the next board session I'd like two slides on the AI roadmap: one on what we shipped this year, one on the 2027 plan and where we need investment. Keep them visual, no walls of text.

Can you get them to me by Thursday 12 November, 12:00? Happy to react to a draft earlier if you have one.

Jonas

Hi Jonas,

Yes, I can do that. I'll draft both slides over the weekend and the start of next week. Do you want the 2027 plan to include headcount, or only platform and infrastructure priorities?

Best,
Alex

> For the next board session I'd like two slides on the AI roadmap...

Platform and infrastructure only, please. Keep headcount out of it for now, we will discuss that separately with Sarah.

One more thing: lead with the customer impact of the fraud-detection model. The board liked that last time. Thursday 12:00 is still the deadline.

Jonas

Hi Alex,

Hope your week is off to a good start. Could we grab 30 minutes this Tuesday, 10 November, at 9:00 AM New York time? I'd like to walk through the integration roadmap for Q1 and agree on next steps for the shared SDK.

I'll send a video link once you confirm. Let me know if another time that day works better.

Thanks,
Daniel Reed
AcmeTech

threads.subject: Payment failed - service will be suspended on 11 Nov

messages.body:
Hi Alex,

We were unable to process your latest subscription payment. The card on file ending in 4417 was declined.

To avoid interruption, please update your payment method before 2026-11-11. If we do not receive payment, your team workspace will be suspended on that date and shared documents will become read-only.

You can update your card in the billing section of your account settings.

Thanks,
NoteKeeper Billing

Team,

Draft postmortem for the 4 Nov inference cluster failover is below. Summary: the primary node pool lost its health probe at 13:12, the failover took 19 minutes instead of 2 because the runbook was out of date, and about 3% of scoring requests timed out.

Root cause: a certificate rotation that was not applied to the standby pool. Please add your comments by tomorrow.

Priya

Thanks Priya. I would add that our alert only fired after 6 minutes, which delayed the first response. We should tighten the threshold on the health probe alert and add a synthetic check on the standby pool.

I can take the alert change this sprint.

Lars

Thanks both. Agree with Lars on alerting. The runbook gap is on me, since my team owns the failover docs. I will update it with the new certificate steps.

Priya, can you list the action items with owners and dates so we can track them?

Best,
Alex

Action items:

1. Lars: tighten health probe alert threshold, due 2026-11-11.
2. Priya: add synthetic check on standby pool, due 2026-11-12.
3. Alex: publish the updated failover runbook with certificate steps, due Friday 2026-11-13.
4. Priya: schedule a failover drill in December.

Let me know if any date is a problem.

Priya

Dates work for me. I will also link the runbook from the alert description once Alex has published it, so on-call engineers land on the right page. I will also review the postmortem draft once more and flag any remaining wording that blames individuals rather than process, so we keep the final version blameless.

Lars

Hi Marcus,

Thanks for the draft proposal. Our main concern is price: the reserved capacity rate is about 12% above what we see from other providers. Can you improve it for a 24-month commitment?

We would also like a termination clause after 12 months, or at least some flexibility to scale down if our workloads change. Our board is cautious about long fixed commitments this year.

Best,
Alex

Hi Alex,

For a 24-month term we can reduce the rate by 6%. A 12-month termination clause is harder, but we could offer a step-down option after month 12 where you can reduce capacity by up to 25%.

Would that be workable?

Marcus

Marcus,

The step-down helps, but 6% is still short. If you can reach 9% and keep the step-down at 30%, I can recommend it internally. We also need a 99.9% uptime SLA with service credits, and a clear definition of what counts as downtime, so that we do not argue about it later.

Best,
Alex

Alex,

I got approval for 8% and a 25% step-down. On the SLA, we can commit to 99.9% with credits of 10% of the monthly fee per breach.

This is close to our best and final. Let me know your view.

Marcus

Marcus,

Better, thank you. I'm discussing it internally this week. Can you confirm the 8% holds for 30 days and that credits apply from the first breach?

If both hold, I will take the proposal to Sarah and our legal team and come back to you with a decision as soon as I can. I want to avoid surprises at signing.

Best,
Alex

Alex,

Confirmed on both points. The offer stays open for 30 days, with credits from the first breach. I have also asked legal to send you the final contract wording so you can review it in parallel.

My finance team needs a decision by Wednesday 2026-11-11 to lock the quarter's allocation. Can you tell me whether you'll sign on these terms? If anything is still open on your side, call me today and we will sort it out quickly.

Marcus
